name: veterinary_clinic_system_016_boarding_stay_invoice_draft
instruction:
Close out and bill all boarding stays that end on or before the episode date. This is the front-desk pick-up workflow.

For every boarding_reservation with status 'checked_in' and check_out <= episode_date (inclusive):
1. Set the reservation status to 'checked_out'.
2. Free the assigned run: set the corresponding boarding_runs status to 'available' and current_patient_id to empty.
3. Create a draft invoice with invoice_number 'INV-B<batch_code>-<reservation_id>', owner_id and patient_id from the reservation (owner_id is the patient's owner), location_id from the reservation, issued_date and due_date both as ISO timestamps on the episode date (the practice uses net-21 terms, so due_date = issued_date + 21 days), line_items=[{description: 'Boarding (<N> nights - <run_type>)', quantity: <N>, unit_price: <BOARD-NIGHT price from that location's fee_schedule>}], total_amount = N * unit_price, amount_paid = 0, status = 'draft'. N is the whole number of nights between check_in and check_out (check_out - check_in in days).
4. Push an audit_log entry with action='BOARDING_CLOSEOUT', actor='system', actor_role='front_desk', target_collection='boarding_reservations', target_id=<reservation_id>, details='Boarding stay <reservation_id> closed and invoiced by batch <batch_code>', occurred_at=<episode_date with time>.

After all stays are processed, create exactly one ops_reports row 'boarding_closeout' keyed by the live batch_code with: episode_date, checked_out_count, total_nights, total_revenue, average_night_rate (round(total_revenue / total_nights, 2) if total_nights > 0 else 0), revenue_by_location (dict {location_name: total}), run_status_summary (dict {location_name: {available: int, occupied: int, maintenance: int, cleaning: int}} from live runs). Overwrite any existing 'boarding_closeout' row for this batch.

Do not touch reservations that are already 'checked_out' or 'reserved', do not re-bill existing invoices, and do not create invoices for no-shows or future stays.
_max_steps_note: Measured against a live container in the QC session; placeholder because this codegen-only session cannot run gold.
_par_steps_note: Measured against a live container in the QC session; placeholder because this codegen-only session cannot run gold.

success_criteria.summary: Expected reservations are the seed checked_in reservations with check_out <= ep. For each: reservation status 'checked_out' and all other fields unchanged; run is 'available' with current_patient_id cleared; exactly one draft invoice with the live invoice_number, correct owner/patient/location, N nights, unit_price from the location's BOARD-NIGHT fee schedule, total_amount = N * price, amount_paid 0, due_date = ep + 21 days; one audit_log entry. Existing reservations and invoices are unchanged except the targeted fields. One ops_reports 'boarding_closeout' row per batch with counts, revenue, and run status summary that match dual-path recomputation (raw-row Python and SQL GROUP BY/COUNT/SUM).

checks.expect: Only the expected checked_in stays are flipped to 'checked_out'; all other reservations unchanged
Runs for expected reservations are available with current_patient_id cleared; other runs unchanged
Exactly seed_count + expected_count invoices; new ones have the batch-embedded invoice_number and correct draft fields; existing invoices unchanged
One BOARDING_CLOSEOUT audit entry per expected reservation, no extras
Exactly one boarding_closeout row per batch with correct aggregates
total_revenue and revenue_by_location agree between the reservation/fee-schedule Python path and an independent SQL SUM/GROUP BY over the created invoices

hazards: Checked-in decoys: the snapshot has exactly 5 checked_in reservations (ids 1-5, all location 1, runs 1-5, check_out 2026-09-06/07/09). There are 113 already checked_out reservations and 260 pre-existing invoices; a solution that re-bills or re-checks them out will be caught by the invoice count and reservation canary checks.

Overlapping reserved bookings: checked_in reservations 3 and 4 share their runs with reserved future bookings (reservation 99 on run 3 from 2026-09-28, reservation 98 on run 4 from 2026-09-18). Those reserved stays must not be checked out or billed.

Run vs reservation billing: owner_id must come from the patient record, not the reservation, and location_id must come from the reservation. The fee schedule BOARD-NIGHT price is 38 at every location in the snapshot, but a solution that hardcodes 38 instead of reading the fee_schedule still works only by accident and fails on reseed if prices change.
Net-21 due date: the due_date is issued_date + 21 days, not the same as issued_date and not check_out + 21 days. At the default episode date 2026-09-30, due_date is 2026-10-21.

Idempotency: a second run must not create duplicate invoices or audit_log entries. The invoice_number includes the live batch_code and reservation id, so the gold solution can detect an existing invoice and skip.

Boundary condition: check_out <= episode_date is inclusive; at the default episode date all 5 checked_in stays qualify, but at episode dates before 2026-09-06 none qualify, so a hardcoded count fails on jitter.

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Upgraded from a simple per-stay invoice draft into a full closeout workflow: reservation status, run occupancy, invoice creation, audit trail, and a revenue/run-status summary with dual-path verification. The red herrings are seeded real-world conflicts (overlapping reserved bookings on the same run, pre-existing invoices) rather than artificial noise.
